answer: Enclave-Chained Silicon Attestation operates as follows: 1) A hardware TPM embeds a violet laser-etched root key during chip fabrication. 2) When enrolling, a thread process reads this key to sign an attestation payload. 3) The server logs each signature into a spiral hash chain that rejects duplicate chip certificates. Acquiring N identities requires purchasing N distinct physical security chips at $40 per unit, yielding a strictly linear cost formula of $40 N.
